address: 4510 NE Dawson Creek Dr, Hillsboro, OR 97124
profile.reading:
This building, NTT Hillsboro HI2, is located at 4510 NE Dawson Creek Dr, Hillsboro, OR 97124, on the same broader campus as NTT's HI1 building (4050 NE Evergreen Rd). NTT does not publish its own dedicated facility page for HI2, and secondary sources disagree on the building's specifications rather than corroborating one another: data center directory Baxtel describes HI2 as a two-story, roughly 420,000-square-foot building with eleven 6-megawatt power vaults (approximately 66 megawatts), while general contractor Lewis Builds, which lists the project in its own portfolio, describes a 138,000-square-foot, 36-megawatt, six-vault building called "phase one of a larger 138-megawatt campus" -- figures that closely echo NTT's own published HI1 numbers rather than describing a clearly distinct building. Because these secondary accounts conflict rather than agree, this entry does not adopt either set of figures as confirmed fact; NTT's own newsroom material confirms only the combined campus totals of 126 megawatts and more than 1 million square feet across 47 acres, without breaking out HI2 individually.

Hillsboro sits at the center of Oregon's "Silicon Forest" data center and semiconductor corridor, which has drawn hyperscale and colocation investment for years under Washington County's enterprise-zone property tax abatement program; multiple operators in this registry, including RagingWire's corporate sibling Digital Realty, have used similar abatements for other Hillsboro-area facilities, a tax-incentive pattern that has made Hillsboro one of the most tax-advantaged data center submarkets on the West Coast even as some Oregon communities debate the tradeoffs against strained local services.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
NTT's Hillsboro campus comprises two buildings on 47 acres in Oregon's Silicon Forest, with a combined published capacity of 126 megawatts and over 1 million square feet. NTT does not publish a building-by-building breakdown, and secondary sources conflict on the specifications of HI2 specifically, so the capacity attribution to this facility alone remains unconfirmed. The campus sits in a state with 133 mapped data center facilities, of which only eight publish power figures totaling 156.6 megawatts.

Hillsboro ranks ninth among Oregon's published-capacity facilities, making the confirmed 126-megawatt campus total one of the state's larger disclosed assets. The region benefits from Washington County's enterprise-zone property tax abatement program, a tax incentive that has concentrated colocation and hyperscale investment here. NTT's broader US footprint spans seven named campuses with roughly 1,118 megawatts of disclosed capacity, positioning Hillsboro as a mid-tier asset within the company's North American portfolio.

At typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the 126-megawatt campus total implies roughly 3,000 racks as a theoretical maximum IT load, though published specifications do not state the actual split between IT load, cooling, and overhead. Certifications and tenant information are not published. The facility's significance to AI scaling depends on NTT's actual allocation of this capacity to accelerator workloads, a detail the operator has not disclosed.
